'''''Encephalartos senticosus''''' is a species of [[cycad]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Zamiaceae]] native to the [[Lebombo Mountains]] of [[Mozambique]], [[Eswatini]] (Swaziland), and the [[KwaZulu-Natal]] province of [[South Africa]]. Prior to its description in 1996, ''Encephalartos senticosus'' had been confused with the closely related and [[sympatry|sympatric]] ''[[Encephalartos lebomboensis]]''.<ref name="vorst1996">{{cite journal|author=Pieter Johannes Vorster|year=1996|title=''Encephalartos senticosus'' (Zamiaceae): a new species from northern KwaZulu-Natal and Swaziland|journal=South African Journal of Botany|volume=62|issue=2 |pages=76–79|doi=10.1016/S0254-6299(15)30594-9 |url=http://www.cycad.org/documents/descriptions/Encephalartos/Encephalartos-senticosus.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.plantzafrica.com/plantefg/encephsenti.htm |title=''Encephalartos senticosus'' Vorster |work=PlantZAfrica |author=M. S. Mothogoane |date=September 2011 |publisher=South African National Biodiversity Institute}}</ref> Both species are commonly known as the '''Lebombo cycad'''.<ref name="ARKive">{{cite web|url=http://www.arkive.org/lebombo-cycad/encephalartos-senticosus/|title=Lebombo cycad (''Encephalartos senticosus'')|publisher=ARKive|access-date=December 10, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131215063647/http://www.arkive.org/lebombo-cycad/encephalartos-senticosus/|archive-date=2013-12-15}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
''Encephalartos senticosus'' is classified in the [[genus]] ''[[Encephalartos]]'' of the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Zamiaceae]]. It was originally included with the closely related ''[[Encephalartos lebomboensis]]'' but was separated as a new species in 1996 by the South African botanist Pieter Johannes Vorster.<ref name="vorst1996"/><ref name=Reynolds/>

''Encephalartos senticosus'' can be distinguished from ''Encephalartos lebomboensis'' primarily by the shape of their cone scales. ''Encephalartos lebomboensis'' male cones are sessile and usually solitary while ''Encephalartos senticosus'' male cones are stalked and in groups of three or four per stem.<ref name=Reynolds>{{cite web |url=http://www.plantzafrica.com/plantefg/encephlebomb.htm |title=''Encephalartos lebomboensis'' |author=Yvonne Reynolds |date=April 2003 |publisher=South Africa National Biodiversity Institute |access-date=December 10, 2013 |archive-date=May 26, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130526180124/http://www.plantzafrica.com/plantefg/encephlebomb.htm }}</ref>

==Description==
''Encephalartos senticosus'' is very similar in appearance to ''Encephalartos lebomboensis''. It has a trunk that is up to {{convert|4|m|abbr=on}} tall and {{convert|30|cm|abbr=on}} thick. It usually suckers at the base, leading to the formation of clumps. The leaves are stiff and straight, usually about {{convert|110|to|150|cm|abbr=on}} in length. The leaflets are glossy and dark green in color, usually {{convert|12|to|18|cm|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|1.4|to|2|cm|abbr=on}} wide. They are narrowly ovate in shape with serrated edges (although rarely, they may be entire). They are set opposite each other at an angle of about 135°, and slant at a 30° angle from the central [[rachis]] towards the tip of the leaf. They are spaced {{convert|2|to|3.5|cm|abbr=on}} from each other at the middle, becoming smaller in size towards the base, with the basal-most leaflets being reduced to prickles.<ref name="vorst1996"/>

''Encephalartos senticosus'' is a [[Dioecy|dioecious]] species, that is, with separate male and female plants. Male specimens produce three or four very narrowly ovoid cones which are set on stalks up to {{convert|10|cm|abbr=on}} long. They are around {{convert|30|to|50|cm|abbr=on}} long and up to {{convert|10|cm|abbr=on}} in diameter. They are orange to yellowish-orange in color. Female specimens also produce two to three barrel-shaped cones, about {{convert|45|cm|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|22|cm|abbr=on}} in diameter. They are pale yellow in color. The seeds have bright red [[sarcotesta]].<ref name="vorst1996"/>

==Distribution==
''Encephalartos senticosus'' is found in the [[Lebombo Mountains]] at altitudes of {{convert|300|-|800|m}}, along the borders of [[South Africa]], [[Swaziland]], and [[Mozambique]]. It is mostly found from south of the [[Pongolapoort Dam|Pongolapoort (Jozini) Dam]] of northern [[KwaZulu-Natal]] to a few kilometers north of the town of [[Siteki]]. Its range overlaps with ''Encephalartos lebomboensis'' in the north.<ref name="iucn status 12 November 2021" /><ref name="vorst1996"/>

==Conservation==
The number of ''Encephalartos senticosus'' growing in the wild is believed to have declined by more than 30% in the last 60 years. It is estimated that about 5,000 to 10,000 specimens of ''Encephalartos senticosus'' are left. The [[IUCN Red List of Threatened Species]] lists it as being "[[Vulnerable species|Vulnerable]]" mainly due to illegal harvesting of the wild plants.<ref name="iucn status 12 November 2021" /> They are commonly cultivated as ornamentals, as well as being sometimes used in [[traditional medicine]].<ref name="vorst1996"/><ref name="cous">{{cite journal|author1=S.R. Cousins |author2=V.L. Williams |author3=E.T.F. Witkowski |year=2012|title=Uncovering the cycad taxa (''Encephalartos'' species) traded for traditional medicine in Johannesburg and Durban, South Africa|journal=South African Journal of Botany|volume=78|pages=129–138|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/232722690|doi=10.1016/j.sajb.2011.06.001|doi-access=free}}</ref> It is listed in [[CITES#Appendix I|Appendix I]] of the CITES Appendices.<ref name="iucn status 12 November 2021" />
